title:
Solvation Cluster Engineering
of Non-Fluorinated Ethers
toward High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
Abstract
Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) can provide high energy density for next-generation energy storage, yet their cycle life remains limited by interfacial incompatibility between electrolyte species and electrodes. Conventional electrolytes based on polar or fluorinated solvents often suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, high cost, and even environmental concerns. Herein, we rationally modulate the polarity and coordination ability of nonfluorinated solvents and report a fluorine-free host–guest synergy electrolyte (HGSE) constructed by tailoring the intermolecular interaction between a long-chain multidentate ether and a monodentate ether solvent. The weak Hδ+–Oδ− intermolecular interaction between these solvents tunes the electrolyte coordination ability and solvation cluster size, leading to a contact ion pair-dominated solvation cluster structure with enhanced ionic conductivity. Meanwhile, the optimized solvation cluster in HGSE promotes anion decomposition while suppressing electrode side reactions, resulting in anion-derived LiF-rich interphases and minimized cathode cracking. More notably, the HGSE electrolyte enables a Li||NCM811 pouch cell to deliver a high energy density of 472.5 Wh kg–1, while a 20 Ah-level anode-free Cu||Ni90 pouch cell with a lean electrolyte (1.5 g Ah–1) achieves a superior energy density of 525 Wh kg–1 with 71.6% capacity retention over 120 cycles. These findings elucidate the role of intermolecular interactions and solvation cluster engineering in high-energy and sustainable LMBs.

title:
Direct Identification
and Quantification of Peptide
Biomarkers in 20% Human Serum Using a Solid-State Nanopore Platform
and Machine Learning
content:
Abstract
The early detection of disabling or life-threatening diseases remains a major challenge in healthcare and relies on the direct identification of disease-specific protein and peptide biomarkers in biological fluids. Here, we establish a polymer-engineered solid-state nanopore platform for the direct electrical identification and quantification of peptide biomarkers in 20% human serum. A semidilute polyethylene glycol network generates an osmotic driving force that promotes peptide capture while screening nonspecific interactions responsible for nanopore clogging. We combine this strategy based on polymer physics with machine-learning-assisted digital serum cleaning to overcome the complexity of biological samples. This method thus allows for the extraction of peptide-specific electrical fingerprints from the serum background. As a proof of concept, we investigate three closely related kinin biomarkers: bradykinin (BK), des-Arg9-bradykinin (DABK), and Lys-bradykinin (LBK), which differ by only one or two terminal amino acids. Despite their high structural similarity, each peptide generates a distinct electrical signature, allowing reliable single-molecule discrimination in both buffer and serum. The platform further identifies and quantifies these biomarkers in mixtures of varying composition in 20% serum. More broadly, this work establishes a general strategy for the direct electrical decoding of closely related peptide biomarkers in clinically relevant biofluids.

title:
Interlayer Mobility
Control of 2D-Layered Crystals
for Delamination of Nanosheets
content:
Abstract
To maintain consistent properties of delaminated two-dimensional nanosheets, mild methods to preserve large lateral sizes and crystallinity during the delamination of bulk crystals are desired. This study introduces a gentle, solution-based on-substrate delamination strategy that avoids forming colloidal free-standing nanosheets by postponing the delamination process until the materials are deposited on the substrate, thereby preventing physical fragmentation in solution. By comparing cone-type and cylinder-type molecular intercalates (oleylamine and hexadecylamine), we identify interlayer mobility as a governing parameter for delamination in intercalation-accessible layered crystals, eliminating the need for external energy input such as sonication. Operando microscopic analyses reveal the importance of the gas–liquid interface during the evaporation process of drop-cast samples, which induces shear forces necessary for delamination. Application to a range of layered oxides and chalcogenides (HNb3O8, HTaMoO6, HTiNbO5, MoO3, V2O5, and TiS2) illustrates the transferability of this working principle across chemically distinct layered materials sharing sufficient interlayer adaptability. These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that controlling interlayer mobility through molecular engineering provides an alternative route to producing large-area, high-quality 2D nanosheets.

title:
Statistically
Guided Electrodeposition of NiFe Electrocatalysts
for Alkaline Oxygen Evolution Reaction
content:
Abstract
Scalable control of NiFe electrodeposition is essential for developing efficient alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes. Here, response surface methodology coupled with a rotatable central composite design was used to simultaneously quantify the effects of deposition current density, deposition temperature, and bath Ni2+/Fe2+ molar ratio on the overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 (η10) and Tafel slope. Bath composition and deposition temperature were the dominant factors, whereas deposition current density was not statistically significant for η10 within the investigated low-current-density range. Multiresponse optimization identified 8.58 mA cm–2, 39 °C, and a bath Ni2+/Fe2+ molar ratio of 1.88 as the optimum deposition conditions. Experimental validation using independently prepared electrodes yielded η10 = 235 mV and a Tafel slope of 69 mV dec–1 in 1 M KOH. The validated electrode consisted predominantly of γ-(Ni,Fe) with a bulk composition of Ni53.6Fe46.4. Electrochemical impedance analysis revealed a regime-dependent relationship between charge-transfer resistance and Tafel behavior, indicating coupled contributions of interfacial charge transfer and surface kinetics to the observed OER performance. The electrode retained 70.9% of its initial anodic response after 1000 cycles and sustained chronopotentiometric operation for 70 h at 10 mA cm–2. After the stronger early stage potential evolution, the 20–70 h interval showed a net increase of 3.3 mV, corresponding to a drift rate of 0.066 mV h–1. Post-OER FESEM showed retained lamellar regions together with localized morphological reorganization, while AAS of the unfiltered post-test electrolyte detected total Fe and Ni concentrations of 1.82 and 1.42 mg/L, respectively. These results demonstrate that the statistically optimized NiFe electrode combines favorable laboratory-scale OER performance with sustained long-term electrochemical operation, while post-test characterization reveals measurable material evolution during extended anodic polarization. Overall, this study establishes a statistically validated framework for linking multivariable NiFe electrodeposition conditions with precursor characteristics and laboratory-scale OER performance.

title:
Quasi-Zero-Strain High-Voltage P2-Type Na 2/3 Li 1/6 Ni 1/3 Mn 1/2 O 2  Cathodes
Enabled by Capacity-Strain Balance
content:
Abstract
Deep sodium extraction/insertion in Mn-based P2-type layered cathodes usually induces undesired lattice strain, transition-metal layer gliding, and irreversible phase transitions, which limit their high-voltage cycling stability. Here, Li incorporation is employed to construct P2–Na2/3Li1/6Ni1/3Mn1/2O2 and regulate the capacity-strain balance for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries. By introducing electrochemically inactive Li while maintaining the Ni content, the local transition-metal-layer environment is modified, enabling stable Na+ storage within the P2 structure. The obtained cathode delivers a discharge capacity of 107 mAh g–1 and an active-material-level specific energy of 363 Wh kg–1 at 0.1 C, while maintaining 95.23% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 1.0 C within 2.0–4.5 V. More importantly, XRD results reveal a reversible reaction pathway characterized by predominantly solid-solution-like structural evolution with suppressed P2–O2/OP4 phase transition during sodium extraction/insertion, giving a maximum volume change of 1.37%. These results suggest that Li incorporation effectively balances the reversible capacity output and structural strain. The relatively low volume change per unit capacity (0.0128% (mAh g–1)−1) further highlights the advantage of this capacity-strain balance strategy.

title:
Ni 3 Se 2 @NiFe Layered Double Hydroxides
for Durable Seawater Electrolysis
content:
Abstract
Developing durable bifunctional electrocatalysts is very crucial for efficient electrochemical water splitting. However, the sluggish reaction kinetics and interface instability restrict their practical application. Herein, we report a hierarchical Ni3Se2@NiFe-LDH heterostructure fabricated via a sequential seed-assisted hydrothermal strategy to ensure strong interfacial adhesion. The metallic Ni3Se2 nanowires serve as a conductive skeleton to facilitate electron transport, while the dense NiFe-LDH shell exposes abundant active sites. In 1.0 M KOH solution, the optimized electrode presents the overpotentials of 78 mV at 10 mA cm–2 for HER and 224 mV at 50 mA cm–2 for OER. Additionally, the assembled electrolyzer requires a cell voltage of 1.69 V at 50 mA cm–2. In alkaline seawater, the electrode requires overpotentials of 117 mV for HER and 273 mV for OER at 10 and 50 mA cm–2, respectively. Remarkably, the composites present robust stability after 150 h of operation in alkaline seawater, demonstrating their viability as electrocatalysts for overall seawater splitting.

title:
Evaluations
of Heterogeneous Dissociation Front Evolution
and Long-Term Production Performance Under Different Depressurization
Schemes in the South China Sea
content:
Abstract
As natural gas hydrate production has transitioned from feasibility validation to industrial development, the engineering objective shifted toward achieving efficient, stable, and economically viable production. There are still some challenges in heterogeneous hydrate geological modeling in optimizing the depressurization strategy. Based on the first hydrate production test in the Shenhu area of the South China Sea, this study constructed a novel heterogeneous geological model by discretizing hydrate heterogeneity. Different depressurization schemes were then developed according to real-time geological responses, including pressure, temperature, and hydrate saturation. Modeling and simulation results showed that different depressurization schemes had little effect on long-term production performance. In contrast, gradient depressurization could better balance dissociation efficiency and sediment stability, and was thereby regarded as the optimal depressurization scheme. In heterogeneous hydrate sediments, the depressurization preferentially propagated rapidly along low-saturation pathways, forming discrete dissociation hotspots, while high-saturation regions retained residual hydrate islands, significantly reducing final gas recovery. The free gas layer (FGL) acted as a high-speed pathway for pressure propagation and a gas buffer, rapidly transmitting the depressurization effect over the long-term of production and providing a sustained heat supply for hydrate dissociation. The challenges posed by heterogeneous hydrate distribution could be overcome by employing fine-scale geological modeling to identify preferential pathways and by developing adaptive depressurization control and multifield coupled models. These findings can provide theoretical guidance for optimizing heterogeneous geological modeling and depressurization strategies for hydrate industrial developments.

title:
Numerical Study on Spray Evaporation Characteristics
of SAFs and Jet A at Elevated Ambient Temperatures
content:
Abstract
Understanding the spray characteristics of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs) is crucial to their safe and efficient utilization. This study employs large-eddy simulations (LES) to investigate the spray and preferential evaporation characteristics of two SAFs and one conventional aviation fuel (Jet A) injected into a combustion chamber via a single-hole injector. The two selected SAFs are hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) and alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) synthetic biofuel, which have distinct component and physical properties compared to Jet A. Two chamber temperatures (473 and 573 K) are considered to investigate fuel effects under weak and strong evaporation conditions. The results show that both SAFs exhibit spray behaviors similar to those of Jet A at 473 K. However, at 573 K, ATJ exhibits the shortest penetration length due to its high proportion of low-boiling-point components, while HEFA shows a much longer penetration. A strong preferential evaporation effect is observed for all fuels at both temperatures, with greater impact on vapor component distribution at low temperatures but on droplet composition at high temperatures. Notably, the distillation curve alone fails to predict the penetration length differences among the fuels. These results suggest that the volatility distribution of fuel components, i.e., the relative proportions of low-, intermediate-, and high-boiling components, plays a significant role in determining spray behavior, particularly at high temperatures.

title:
Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Shale Adsorption
Capacity after Supercritical CO 2  Soaking
content:
Abstract
Supercritical CO2 (scCO2) soaking can alter the pore structure, mineral composition, and surface properties of shale, thereby affecting its adsorption capacity. Therefore, accurate prediction of shale adsorption capacity after scCO2 soaking is of great significance for evaluating CO2 geological sequestration potential and shale gas recovery performance. In this study, a database of the amount of CO2 adsorbed by shale was collected, which contained 315 data points from 26 shale samples before and after scCO2 soaking. Eight input variables were selected, including adsorption pressure, adsorption temperature, soaking pressure, soaking temperature, soaking time, quartz content, clay content, and total organic carbon (TOC) content, with CO2 adsorption capacity as the output variable. Four machine learning models, namely multilayer perceptron (MLP), support vector regression (SVR), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), were constructed and optimized to predict the shale adsorption capacity. The results showed that XGBoost exhibited the best predictive performance among the four models, achieving an R2 of 0.9772 on the test set. To address the insufficient predictive performance of XGBoost under high soaking pressure conditions, an XGBoost–Langmuir model was developed by inversely determining the Langmuir adsorption parameters from XGBoost predictions. Compared with the XGBoost and Langmuir models, the XGBoost-Langmuir model significantly improved prediction accuracy and reduced errors under high soaking pressures. Analyses of SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values and SHAP interaction values indicated that clay content exhibited asymmetric contributions to model predictions, adsorption temperature generally contributed negatively, and quartz content contributed positively, while the contribution of TOC to model predictions was associated with its interactions with pressure conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed XGBoost-Langmuir model enhanced the reliability of predicting shale adsorption capacity after scCO2 soaking and revealed the changes in adsorption-controlling factors induced by scCO2 treatment.

title:
Dual Effects
of Water on CO 2  Adsorption
in Silica Mesopores: Interfacial Promotion versus Volume-Limited Inhibition
content:
Abstract
Water is ubiquitous in natural and engineered porous media and plays a critical role in regulating CO2 adsorption in carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) systems. Previous studies report contradictory effects of water, ranging from suppression to enhancement of CO2 uptake, indicating that the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigate CO2 adsorption in silica mesopores with varying water contents using molecular simulations under thermodynamic conditions relevant to three typical CCUS scenarios. The results suggest two distinct adsorption regimes controlled by the thermodynamic state of CO2. Under gaseous conditions, CO2 uptake is governed by an interfacial-area-controlled regime and exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic response to water content, with enhancement arising from abundant water interfacial area within low-density regions. In contrast, under supercritical conditions, CO2 uptake is governed by an accessible-volume-controlled regime and decreases monotonically with increasing water content. Similar trends are observed in both hydrophilic and hydrophobic pores, although the spatial distribution of water differs substantially between them. These findings provide molecular-scale insights into the contrasting effects of water on CO2 adsorption and may inform future investigations of water management in CO2 capture, mineral carbonation, and geological storage.

title:
Mechanistic Insights into Chemical-Assisted Steam
Injection: Pore-Scale Evidence for More Efficient and Lower-Carbon
Heavy Oil Recovery
content:
Abstract
Steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) is the primary method for in situ extraction of heavy oil and bitumen in Canada. However, it (as well as other steam injection methods) suffers from low efficiency, high water and energy consumption, and significant environmental impact. Adding chemicals to steam offers a potential solution by enhancing oil recovery while reducing carbon emissions through lower steam usage. Our previous studies have shown that deep eutectic solvents (DES) and thermally stable nonionic surfactants improve steam chamber sweep efficiency and microscopic displacement efficiency, respectively. However, their mechanisms and effects in porous media, especially at the pore scale, remain unclear. This study explores the microdisplacement mechanisms of these chemical additives. A porous medium model was created by packing glass beads between two plexiglass plates, which was then saturated with heavy oil at a slow injection rate. The research focused on steam chamber growth dynamics, physicochemical changes at the oil-steam-water-rock interface, and their impact on oil drainage. By comparing oil recovery efficiency, energy efficiency, and carbon intensity of SAGD with and without chemical additives, the effects of DES (formulated in our laboratories and named as DES 11) and Novelfroth (a commercial nonionic surfactant) on steam injection efficiency were evaluated. The results demonstrate that DES 11 and Novelfroth 190 enhance the recovery rate by 31.1% and 37%, respectively, while reducing carbon emission intensity to one-third to one-half of conventional SAGD. However, their underlying mechanisms differ. Also, the introduction of these chemical additives significantly altered the state of residual oil compared to the base case. Ultimately, the improvement in oil recovery per unit of steam injected in the chemical cases was quantified and linked to a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions during steam injection.

title: A 2.2 V Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Enabled by Passive pH Decoupling
content:
Abstract
Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.

title: Current Density as a Critical Factor Governing the Cycle Life of Polysulfide-Based Redox Flow Batteries
content:
Abstract
Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.

title: Operando  Raman Spectroscopy-Guided 24-Hour Aging Assessment of Activated Carbon Positive Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Capacitors
content:
Abstract
While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.

title: Tailoring Manganese Oxide Cathodes via Basic-Medium Synthesis for Enhanced Zn 2+  Storage: Unraveling Interfacial Kinetics and Transport Limitations
content:
Abstract
Manganese-based aqueous rechargeable zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are emerging as highly viable alternatives to lithium-ion systems for grid-scale energy storage, driven by their cost-effectiveness, intrinsic safety, and high theoretical capacity. However, their commercial deployment is currently hindered by performance degradation stemming from structural instability during prolonged cycling. This study systematically investigates the influence of the synthesis environment on the structural evolution and electrochemical performance of manganese oxide cathodes. By manipulating the reaction medium, we demonstrate that alkaline environments yield Hollandite-type NaxMn8O16 (h-MO) with hierarchical flower-like morphology, whereas near-neutral conditions produce aggregated Mn3O4 (MO) spherical particles. Comprehensive characterization via XRD, ICP-OES, Raman spectroscopy, XPS, SEM, TEM, and BET corroborates this distinct phase and morphological divergence. Electrochemical evaluations reveal that the h-MO cathode delivers a superior reversible capacity (252 mAh·g–1 at 50 mA·g–1) compared to MO counterpart (52 mAh·g–1). Furthermore, h-MO exhibits good cycling stability, displaying an 8% capacity increase over 160 cycles at 200 mA g–1. Ex situ XRD and SEM analyses reveal a reversible H+/Zn2+ co-storage mechanism accompanied by reversible zinc hydroxide sulfate formation. Crucially, operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) coupled with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis was employed to deconvolute the dynamic electrochemical processes of the h-MO cathode during cycling. This advanced diagnostic approach provides profound insights into the evolution of interfacial charge-transfer and ion-transport kinetics. These findings highlight the importance of synthesis-driven control in tailoring manganese oxide cathodes and offer guidance for the rational design of advanced AZIB systems.

title: Thiophene π-Bridge Fluorination Enables Conformational Locking and Molecular Packing for High-Performance TPD-Based Nonfullerene Acceptors
content:
Abstract
Engineering the π-bridge of nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) is an effective strategy for regulating their optoelectronic properties and molecular packing; however, the influence of thiophene π-bridge fluorination on charge transport and recombination remains insufficiently understood. Here, two thieno[3,4-c]pyrrole-4,6-dione (TPD)-based NFAs, TC8 and TFC8, incorporating thiophene π-bridges bearing alkyl-substituents and both alkyl- and fluorine substituents, respectively, were designed and synthesized to elucidate the effect of π-bridge fluorination on organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Fluorination gives rise to intramolecular S··F noncovalent interactions, inducing conformational locking that enhances intermolecular π–π stacking while modulating the optical absorption and frontier energy levels. Consequently, TFC8-based OSCs showed a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 12.7%, more than twice that of TC8-based devices (5.8%), accompanied by improvements in the short-circuit current density (JSC) and fill factor (FF). Detailed device analyses revealed that fluorination of the π-bridge lowers both the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy levels, leading to more favorable energy-level alignment with the donor PM6 for efficient charge separation. Moreover, the PM6:TFC8 blend film exhibited enhanced and well-balanced charge transport, suppressed bimolecular and trap-assisted recombination, and improved molecular ordering, resulting in more efficient charge extraction and photovoltaic performance. This work demonstrates that thiophene π-bridge fluorination is an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular packing, charge transport, and recombination, providing useful guidelines for the development of high-performance NFAs.

title: Electrostatic Assembly of Self-Encapsulated Composite Electrets for High-Stability Droplet Energy Harvesting
content:
Abstract
Electret materials are vital for low-frequency mechanical energy conversion; however, their practical outdoor deployment is severely restricted by moisture-induced charge decay and environmental screening. Herein, an electrostatic assembly technology is reported to construct a robust composite electret film featuring a self-encapsulated inner charge layer. By bringing a corona-charged fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) film into intimate contact with an uncharged secondary dielectric layer, interfacial charge redistribution and dielectric polarization establish a persistent interfacial electric field, generating a maximum interfacial shear holding strength of 3.50 N/cm2. Following this electrostatic assembly via corona-injected charges, the resulting self-encapsulated structure effectively shields the active charge carriers from moisture and screening. Based on this film, a composite droplet electret generator (C-DEG) is developed. Utilizing a transistor-like “bulk effect”, the C-DEG delivers a peak power of 0.25 mW at a 2 MΩ load under a single-droplet impact, maintaining a stable output for over 6000 s. This work provides a stable, packaging-free paradigm for resilient self-powered systems.

title: Mechanically Balanced Elastomer-Filled 3D LAGP Framework Composite Solid Electrolytes for Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
Abstract
Ceramic framework-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) because they integrate continuous ion-transport pathways with improved electrode/electrolyte contact. However, the role of the mechanical properties of the soft phase infiltrated into the ceramic framework remains insufficiently understood. Herein, we design elastomer-filled CSEs by infiltrating a fluorinated elastomer electrolyte into a porous natrum super ionic conductor (NASICON)-type Li1.5Al0.5Ge1.5(PO4)3 (LAGP) framework. The crosslinking density of the elastomer phase is controlled by varying the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) content, enabling systematic tuning of toughness, elastic recovery, interfacial adhesion, and compressive stiffness while maintaining comparable ionic conductivity. Although all CSEs exhibit ionic conductivities in the 10–4 S cm–1 range, their Li metal interfacial stability and half-cell performance strongly depend on the mechanical balance of the elastomer phase. Insufficient crosslinking leads to poor toughness and adhesion, whereas excessive crosslinking enhances adhesion but compromises recovery, toughness, and stiffness. The optimized P20 + LAGP exhibits an ionic conductivity of 0.18 mS cm–1, adhesion energy of 44.1 J m–2, and compressive modulus of 0.85 MPa, enabling stable Li plating/stripping over 100 h and 91.4% capacity retention after 100 cycles in NMC811|CSE|Li half cells. In contrast, the other CSEs show inferior cycling stability, with capacity retentions below 80%.

title: High-Throughput Discovery of Cu 0 /Cu δ+  Interfacial Catalysts for CO 2  Electroreduction toward C 2+  Products
content:
Abstract
Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) toward C2+ products offers a sustainable route for producing high-value chemicals, but is limited by the sluggish C–C coupling step. Copper (Cu)-based catalysts are uniquely effective for C2+ products, and their performance is strongly governed by the interplay between Cu0 and Cuδ+ species. Here, we developed a workflow to evaluate Cu compounds by high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations and proposed potential Cu0/Cuδ+ interfacial catalysts for CO2RR to C2+ products. By applying a set of predetermined criteria, we screened 7 promising candidates from 860 Cu compounds, which could be potentially effective in stabilizing Cuδ+ and constructing a Cu0/Cuδ+ interface to facilitate C–C coupling. Notably, we found that the electrochemical stability of Cuδ+ species is governed by the Cu–X bond strength, and Cuδ+ sites coordinated with S, Se, Te, N, and As could exhibit enhanced stability. The difference between *CO adsorption energy on the Cu0 site and *CHO adsorption energy on the Cuδ+ site is expected to be a key descriptor governing C–C coupling at the Cu0/Cuδ+ interface, and ΔG(*CHO@Cuδ+) – ΔG(*CO@Cu0) should be controlled at ∼–0.5 eV. These findings offer fundamental guidance for the design of Cu0/Cuδ+ interfacial catalysts for CO2RR. This work gives a direction for developing promising Cu0/Cuδ+ interfacial catalysts for CO2RR and provides a framework for high-throughput screening of potential interfacial catalysts for other reactions.

title: Oxygen-Assisted Direct Synthesis of Two-Dimensional Ferroelectric Bi 2 SeO 5
content:
Abstract
Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectrics are promising for nonvolatile memory, nanoelectronics, and neuromorphic devices. Among them, bismuth selenite (Bi2SeO5) has recently emerged as a high-performance van der Waals (vdW) ferroelectric oxide. However, its current synthesis mainly relies on the post-oxidation of Bi2O2Se, which complicates the fabrication process and limits its integration potential. Here, we report the oxygen-assisted direct synthesis of 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 nanosheets by regulating the oxygen chemical potential and the resulting relative thermodynamic stability of competing Bi–Se–O phases. The presence of O2 increases the oxygen chemical potential, rendering Bi2SeO5 thermodynamically more stable than Bi2O2Se and enabling its direct growth. The as-grown Bi2SeO5 nanosheets exhibit high crystallinity, uniform composition, well-defined chemical states, and robust in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) ferroelectricity, while temperature-dependent second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements reveal that the non-centrosymmetric phase persists up to approximately 690 K. Lateral and vertical devices further demonstrate stable polarization-controlled resistive switching. This work establishes a direct synthesis route to 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 and provides a foundation for ferroelectric memory and nanoelectronic devices.

title: Hierarchical Magnetic Nanocomposite for the Efficient Sequestration of Perfluorooctanoic Acid and Toxic Metals: Unraveling Multimodal Adsorption Mechanisms
content:
Abstract
Adsorbents that remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) alongside heavy metals typically fail because PFAS capture requires acidic pH while metal capture requires near-neutral pH, and materials optimized for one class perform poorly on the other. We report a magnetically recoverable nanocomposite, Fe3O4@SiO2@Fe-MOF@N-doped carbon quantum dots (Mag–MOF–CQD), that resolves this conflict by spatially segregating the two capture chemistries: a mesoporous Fe-MOF shell binds perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) through electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, while an outer nitrogen-doped carbon-dot layer binds Pb2+ and Hg2+ through inner-sphere coordination. A two-stage pH-swing protocol (utilizing sequential fresh doses of the same material platform) exploits this segregation to remove all three pollutants from a single ternary mixture at 94–99% efficiency, with magnetic recovery in under 30 seconds. In authentic tap water, the material lowers PFOA from 50 ng L–1 to 1.5 ng L–1, below the 4 ng L–1 US EPA drinking-water limit. The Fe-MOF shell also catalyzes in situ photo-Fenton-like defluorination of captured PFOA (72% efficiency under simulated solar light), partially degrading the pollutant rather than merely relocating it. Density functional theory models and spectroscopic analysis suggest that the two active-site classes operate independently, mitigating competitive interference. Mag–MOF–CQD thus combines regulatory-relevant trace removal, multi-pollutant selectivity, and integrated partial destruction in a single recoverable material.

title: Ultralow-Pt Titanium Carbide Anode Electrocatalyst for Durable Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells
content:
Abstract
Sustained operation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) at ultralow Pt loadings is limited by anode degradation: in conventional Pt/C, corrosion of the carbon support and Pt loss drive activity decay while reformate-fed and high-temperature operation add CO poisoning. Replacing the exposed carbon surface with a more robust carbide addresses both limits. Here, we report a titanium carbide (TiC) supported Pt anode in which strong Pt–TiC interactions stabilize Pt as isolated atoms and subnanometer clusters. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show strong Pt binding on both TiC (100) and TiC (111) and spontaneous H2 dissociation at Pt–C interfacial sites. In a phosphoric acid-doped polybenzimidazole (PA-PBI) membrane electrode assembly (MEA) at 150 °C under a CO-containing H2 stream, the 1 wt % Pt/TiC anode delivers a peak power density comparable to a commercial 10 wt % Pt/C reference with four times less Pt and shows no decay over 100 h. At an ultralow loading of 0.015 mgPt cm–2, the catalyst sustains stable power density of 0.16 W cm–2 for ∼100 h in a Nafion-based MEA at 80 °C, corresponding to 10.7 WmgPt–1of anode Pt. These results identify TiC support engineering as a promising strategy for durable low-Pt anodes across low- and high-temperature PEMFCs, with improved performance retention under CO-containing feed at 150 °C.

title: Oxygen Functionalization Enables Magnesium Storage in a TiC 3  Monolayer: A First-Principles Study of Mg Adsorption and Migration
content:
Abstract
Magnesium-ion batteries motivate the search for lightweight hosts with favorable storage energetics and accessible migration paths. We used density-functional theory to study Mg adsorption and migration on pristine and oxygen-functionalized TiC3. Adsorption on the pristine sheet is unfavorable relative to bulk Mg (+0.67 eV), whereas an isolated Mg atom binds at the B2 surface site of the partially oxidized sheet at –0.39 eV. For the sampled configurations, the PBE loading hull follows n = 0 → 1 → 4 → 12, where n is the number of Mg atoms in the Ti16C48O4 cell. The n = 12 endpoint gives a theoretical host-mass capacity of 457 mAh g–1, with voltage plateaus of 0.358, 0.249, and 0.014 V. Dispersion-inclusive relaxation retains a positive n = 4 → 12 insertion voltage, although its value depends on the treatment. Seven-image CI-NEB calculations give dilute B2–B3 surface barriers of 0.699 eV for the O-adjacent P1 path and 1.074 eV for the surface-void P6 path. These results show how oxygen functionalization changes Mg adsorption and the local migration environment. The low anode voltage and moderate dilute migration barrier should be considered together when assessing this model host.

title: Progresses in Potential Spectrally Selective Absorbing Coatings for Ultra-High-Temperature (≥600 °C) Solar Thermal Generation
content:
Abstract
Concentrated solar power (CSP) technology offers advantages including clean operation, zero pollution, high energy conversion efficiency, and the capability of 24-hour continuous power generation via large-capacity thermal energy storage; consequently, its installed capacity has grown dramatically in recent years. Spectrally selective absorbing coatings (SSACs) are the key functional materials for solar-to-thermal conversion, and their optical performance and thermal stability directly determine the power generation efficiency and the service life of CSP systems. Increasing the operating temperature of CSP systems is well known to significantly improve power generation efficiency and reduce costs. Therefore, to support the future development of ultra-high-temperature (≥600 °C) CSP technologies such as supercritical CO2 cycles, exploring potential SSACs that can withstand temperatures above 600 °C and exhibit excellent photothermal conversion efficiency has become a paramount research topic. This work reviews the research progress on the most promising ultra-high-temperature SSACs using a temperature-graded framework covering 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C. It discusses material selection, multilayer configuration, optical performance, thermal stability, and the intrinsic mechanisms underlying coating failure at high temperatures, thereby providing a reference for subsequent research and engineering applications. The practical implications for CSP plant operation are also discussed, including thermal cycling effects, service-life prediction, and the gap between laboratory-scale stability and real-world field performance.

title: Generalization-Oriented Cross-Literature Process Informatics Reveals Transferable but Context-Dependent Fabrication Signals in Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Abstract
Literature-scale databases provide an opportunity to learn fabrication–performance relationships in perovskite solar cells, but conventional device-level validation can confound transferable process information with publication-specific experimental structure. Here, we develop a generalization-oriented process-informatics framework using a provenance-controlled cohort of 41,015 manually extracted devices from 7292 digital object identifier-indexed publications in the NOMAD-hosted Perovskite Solar Cells Database. Material/device descriptors, process-reporting indicators, and actual fabrication variables were analyzed separately using Extreme Gradient Boosting, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, and random forest models under random-row, publication-held-out, and rolling future-year validation. Under random splitting, approximately 97% of test records shared publication identity with training data, substantially inflating apparent predictive performance. Nevertheless, after complete digital object identifier (DOI) separation, adding fabrication descriptors reduced mean absolute prediction error by approximately 0.19–0.20 percentage point in power conversion efficiency (PCE) across all three model families (an incremental gain, not the absolute model error of approximately 3.2 PCE percentage points). The process-related predictive gain was reproduced in two well-supported future-year tests and persisted in complete-case analyses. Among physically defined fabrication-process blocks, solvent-recipe descriptors showed the most reproducible cross-publication and temporal transfer. Their incremental predictive value remained after expanded control for material, formulation, measurement, reporting, and other process variables and after restriction to single-step spin coating. However, exploratory within-publication N,N-dimethylformamide–dimethyl sulfoxide comparisons involving only 22 DOI groups provided insufficient evidence for a common monotonic mixing-ratio response or shared optimum. These results distinguish transferable predictive information from a universal process law and suggest the use of literature-scale process informatics to identify promising process–context relationships for subsequent experimental validation, rather than to prescribe a universal solvent ratio.

title: First-Principles Investigation of Molybdenum Tetraboride Monolayer Interface for Improved Polysulfide Immobilization in Li-S Batteries
content:
Abstract
The shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides is a key challenge for Li–S batteries, leading to loss of sulfur, capacity fading and poor cycling stability. Herein, the MoB4 monolayer has been explored as a host cathode material through DFT calculations. The results show that MoB4 possesses good thermodynamic and dynamic stability, strong adsorption of sulfur and lithium polysulfides and effective polysulfide confinement to suppress the sulfur shuttling effect. In addition, MoB4 is catalytically active for Li2S conversion to facilitate the sulfur redox and improve the reaction kinetics. Good electronic conductivity, favorable conversion energetics and fast diffusion further facilitate sulfur utilization. The results demonstrate that MoB4 is a promising host material for high-performance Li–S batteries.

title: Enhancing Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3  Ionic Conductivity via Microstructural and Average Structural Tuning Induced by Sm 2 O 3  Sintering Additives
content:
Abstract
Currently, further improvement in ionic conductivity remains essential for NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) solid-state electrolytes to enable their practical use in all solid-state batteries. In this study, Sm2O3 was used as a sintering additive for LATP, and its effects on the microstructure, conductivity, and crystal structure of the LATP were investigated. The substantial reduction in LATP grain size and improved grain connectivity increased the grain boundary conductivity by nearly an order of magnitude, yielding a total conductivity of 0.44 mS/cm at 20 °C for the LATP + 9 wt % Sm2O3 co-sintered sample. The diffraction patterns revealed that the Sm2O3 additive reacted with LATP to form SmPO4 and LiTiOPO4 as secondary phases. Combined Rietveld refinement using X-ray and neutron diffraction data revealed that this reaction could increase the Al3+/Ti4+ ratio in the average structure of LATP, which correlated with the reduced activation energy for bulk conduction. These findings demonstrate that Sm2O3 or other rare-earth element oxide additives provide a simple and effective solution for the microstructural tuning and conductivity enhancement of LATP.

title: Enzymatically Active Liposomal Nanobots for the Penetration of Intercellular and Intracellular Barriers
content:
GOx‐powered liposomal nanobots exploit tumor acidity to facilitate deep penetration into multicellular tumor tissue. They overcome lysosomal sequestration through chemo–mechanical escape driven by catalytic membrane destabilization and sustained active motion under confinement. Lysosomal escape subsequently promotes redistribution toward ER‐ and Golgi‐associated compartments and intercellular relay transport, sustaining nanobot trafficking across sequential biological barriers for enhanced drug delivery.








ABSTRACT
Delivery systems for nanomedicine are critical, however, they are restricted by intercellular and intracellular barriers including lysosomal sequestration after cellular uptake, that impede penetration from the tissue to the subcellular level. Here, we report a liposomal nanobot with enzymatic propulsion and drug‐payload capabilities that exhibits tumor microenvironment responsiveness and active penetration, enabling intracellular transport and active lysosomal escape. This nanobot arises from phase‐separated vesicles of liposome and bacterial outer membrane vesicles that possess doxorubicin‐encapsulation capability and are asymmetrically functionalized with glucose oxidase to form a Janus catalytic interface for self‐diffusiophoresis in the presence of glucose. Under mildly acidic conditions, these nanobots display enhanced motility and chemotactic migration toward acidic regions, leveraging pH gradients in the tumor microenvironment to infiltrate tumor spheroids. Once internalized, the nanobots are rapidly captured by lysosomes and subsequently escape, as a plausible chemo–mechanical mechanism involving catalytic membrane perturbation and active motion. Then nanobot‐associated signals redistribute toward ER‐ and Golgi‐associated compartments and persist across successive recipient cells, supporting intercellular relay transport. The encapsulated drug is released within tumor cells, enabling enhanced antitumor efficacy. This nanobot thus demonstrates an active drug delivery system capable of traversing cellular barriers, providing a strategy for precision tumor therapy.
